writeInt64.haxe_doc: Writes a 64-bit signed integer to the byte stream. @param value An integer to write to the byte stream.

endian.haxe_doc: The byte order for the data, either the `BIG_ENDIAN` or `LITTLE_ENDIAN` constant from the Endian class.

objectEncoding.haxe_doc: Used to determine whether the `AMF3` or `AMF0` format is used when writing or reading binary data using the `writeObject()` method. The value is a constant from the ObjectEncoding class.

writeBoolean.haxe_doc:
Writes a Boolean value. A single byte is written according to the `value` parameter, either 1 if `true` or 0 if `false`.
@param value A Boolean value determining which byte is written. If the parameter is `true`, 1 is written; if `false`, 0 is written.

writeBytes.haxe_doc:
Writes a sequence of bytes from the specified byte array, bytes, starting at the byte specified by `offset` (using a zero-based index) with a length specified by `length`, into the file stream, byte stream, or byte array.
If the `length` parameter is omitted, the default length of 0 is used and the entire buffer starting at `offset` is written. If the `offset` parameter is also omitted, the entire buffer is written.
If the `offset` or `length` parameter is out of range, they are clamped to the beginning and end of the bytes array.
@param bytes The byte array to write. @param offset A zero-based index specifying the position into the array to begin writing. @param length An unsigned integer specifying how far into the buffer to write.

writeDouble.haxe_doc:
Writes an IEEE 754 double-precision (64-bit) floating point number.
@param value A double-precision (64-bit) floating point number.

writeFloat.haxe_doc:
Writes an IEEE 754 single-precision (32-bit) floating point number.
@param value A single-precision (32-bit) floating point number.

writeInt.haxe_doc:
Writes a 32-bit signed integer.
@param value A byte value as a signed integer.

writeUnsignedInt.haxe_doc:
Writes a 32-bit unsigned integer.
@param value A byte value as an unsigned integer.

class.haxe_doc:
The IDataOutput interface provides a set of methods for writing binary data. This interface is the I/O counterpart to the IDataInput interface, which reads binary data. The IDataOutput interface is implemented by the FileStream, Socket and ByteArray classes.
All IDataInput and IDataOutput operations are "bigEndian" by default (the most significant byte in the sequence is stored at the lowest or first storage address), and are nonblocking.
Sign extension matters only when you read data, not when you write it. Therefore, you do not need separate write methods to work with `IDataInput.readUnsignedByte()` and `IDataInput.readUnsignedShort()`. In other words:
* Use `IDataOutput.writeByte()` with `IDataInput.readUnsignedByte()` and `IDataInput.readByte()`. * Use `IDataOutput.writeShort()` with `IDataInput.readUnsignedShort()` and `IDataInput.readShort()`.

bytesAvailable.haxe_doc: Returns the number of bytes of data available for reading in the input buffer. User code must call `bytesAvailable` to ensure that sufficient data is available before trying to read it with one of the read methods.

endian.haxe_doc: The byte order for the data, either the `BIG_ENDIAN` or `LITTLE_ENDIAN` constant from the Endian class.

objectEncoding.haxe_doc: Used to determine whether the `AMF3` or `AMF0` format is used when writing or reading binary data using the `readObject()` method. The value is a constant from the ObjectEncoding class.

class.haxe_doc:
The IDataInput interface provides a set of methods for reading binary data. This interface is the I/O counterpart to the IDataOutput interface, which writes binary data.
All IDataInput and IDataOutput operations are "bigEndian" by default (the most significant byte in the sequence is stored at the lowest or first storage address), and are nonblocking. If insufficient data is available, an `EOFError` exception is thrown. Use the `IDataInput.bytesAvailable` property to determine how much data is available to read.
Sign extension matters only when you read data, not when you write it. Therefore you do not need separate write methods to work with `IDataInput.readUnsignedByte()` and `IDataInput.readUnsignedShort()`. In other words:
* Use `IDataOutput.writeByte()` with `IDataInput.readUnsignedByte()` and `IDataInput.readByte()`. * Use `IDataOutput.writeShort()` with `IDataInput.readUnsignedShort()` and `IDataInput.readShort()`.

__allocated.haxe_doc: The number of bytes allocated. May be ~50% larger than `length`.

__length.haxe_doc: An alias for `length`, except guaranteed not to have side effects. This matters in openfljs mode, where setting `length` calls`__resize()`, but setting `__length` does not.

abstract.haxe_doc: The CompressionAlgorithm class defines string constants for the names of compress and uncompress options. These constants are used as values of the `algorithm` parameter of the `ByteArray.compress()` and `ByteArray.uncompress()` methods.

DEFLATE.haxe_doc: Defines the string to use for the deflate compression algorithm.

ZLIB.haxe_doc: Defines the string to use for the zlib compression algorithm.

DEFLATE.haxe_doc: Defines the string to use for the deflate compression algorithm.

ZLIB.haxe_doc: Defines the string to use for the zlib compression algorithm.

exists.haxe_doc:
Returns `true` if `key` has a mapping, `false` otherwise.
If key is `null`, the result is unspecified.

get.haxe_doc:
Returns the current mapping of `key`.
If no such mapping exists, `null` is returned.
Note that a check like `dict.get(key) == null` can hold for two reasons:
1. The Dictionary has no mapping for `key` 2. The Dictionary has a mapping with a value of `null`
If it is important to distinguish these cases, `exists()` should be used.
If `key` is null, the result is unspecified.

keyValueIterator.haxe_doc:
Returns an Iterator over the keys and values of this Dictionary.
The order of values is undefined.

remove.haxe_doc:
Removes the mapping of `key` and returns `true` if such a mapping existed, `false` otherwise.
If `key` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

set.haxe_doc:
Maps `key` to `value`.
If `key` already has a mapping, the previous value disappears.
If `key` is `null`, the result is unspecified.

iterator.haxe_doc:
Returns an Iterator over the keys of this Dictionary.
The order of values is undefined.

each.haxe_doc:
Returns an Iterator over each of the values of this Dictionary.
The order of values is undefined.

indexOf.haxe_doc: Binary search through floatKeys array, which is sorted, to find an index of a given key. If the array doesn't contain such key -1 is returned.

insertSorted.haxe_doc: Insert the key at a proper index in the array and return the index. The array must will remain sorted. The keys are unique so if the key already existis in the array it isn't added but it's index is returned.

abstract.haxe_doc:
The Endian class contains values that denote the byte order used to represent multibyte numbers. The byte order is either bigEndian (most significant byte first) or littleEndian (least significant byte first).
OpenFL content can interface with a server by using the binary protocol of that server, directly. Some servers use the bigEndian byte order and some servers use the littleEndian byte order. Most servers on the Internet use the bigEndian byte order because "network byte order" is bigEndian. The littleEndian byte order is popular because the Intel x86 architecture uses it. Use the endian byte order that matches the protocol of the server that is sending or receiving data.

BIG_ENDIAN.haxe_doc:
Indicates the most significant byte of the multibyte number appears first in the sequence of bytes.
The hexadecimal number 0x12345678 has 4 bytes (2 hexadecimal digits per byte). The most significant byte is 0x12. The least significant byte is 0x78. (For the equivalent decimal number, 305419896, the most significant digit is 3, and the least significant digit is 6).
A stream using the bigEndian byte order (the most significant byte first) writes:
``` 12 34 56 78 ```

LITTLE_ENDIAN.haxe_doc:
Indicates the least significant byte of the multibyte number appears first in the sequence of bytes.
The hexadecimal number 0x12345678 has 4 bytes (2 hexadecimal digits per byte). The most significant byte is 0x12. The least significant byte is 0x78. (For the equivalent decimal number, 305419896, the most significant digit is 3, and the least significant digit is 6).
A stream using the littleEndian byte order (the most significant byte first) writes:
``` 78 56 34 12 ```

BIG_ENDIAN.haxe_doc:
Indicates the most significant byte of the multibyte number appears first in the sequence of bytes.
The hexadecimal number 0x12345678 has 4 bytes (2 hexadecimal digits per byte). The most significant byte is 0x12. The least significant byte is 0x78. (For the equivalent decimal number, 305419896, the most significant digit is 3, and the least significant digit is 6).
A stream using the bigEndian byte order (the most significant byte first) writes:
``` 12 34 56 78 ```

LITTLE_ENDIAN.haxe_doc:
Indicates the least significant byte of the multibyte number appears first in the sequence of bytes.
The hexadecimal number 0x12345678 has 4 bytes (2 hexadecimal digits per byte). The most significant byte is 0x12. The least significant byte is 0x78. (For the equivalent decimal number, 305419896, the most significant digit is 3, and the least significant digit is 6).
A stream using the littleEndian byte order (the most significant byte first) writes:
``` 78 56 34 12 ```

readExternal.haxe_doc:
A class implements this method to decode itself from a data stream by calling the methods of the IDataInput interface. This method must read the values in the same sequence and with the same types as were written by the `writeExternal()` method.
@param input The name of the class that implements the IDataInput interface.

uid.haxe_doc: The user id for the file owner.

size.haxe_doc: The size of the file, in bytes.

rdev.haxe_doc: The device type on which stat resides (special files only).

nlink.haxe_doc: The number of hard links to stat.

mtime.haxe_doc: The last modification time for the file.

mode.haxe_doc: The permission bits of stat. The meaning of the bits is platform dependent.

gid.haxe_doc: The user group id for the file owner.

dev.haxe_doc: The device on which stat resides.

ctime.haxe_doc: The creation time for the file (not all file systems support this).

atime.haxe_doc: The last access time for the file (when enabled by the file system).

typedef.haxe_doc: File information, as given by `sys.FileSystem.stat`.

getContent.haxe_doc:
Retrieves the content of the file specified by `path` as a String.
If the file does not exist or can not be read, an exception is thrown.
`sys.FileSystem.exists` can be used to check for existence.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

getBytes.haxe_doc:
Retrieves the binary content of the file specified by `path`.
If the file does not exist or can not be read, an exception is thrown.
`sys.FileSystem.exists` can be used to check for existence.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

saveContent.haxe_doc:
Stores `content` in the file specified by `path`.
If the file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
If `path` or `content` are null, the result is unspecified.

saveBytes.haxe_doc:
Stores `bytes` in the file specified by `path` in binary mode.
If the file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
If `path` or `bytes` are null, the result is unspecified.

read.haxe_doc:
Returns an `FileInput` handle to the file specified by `path`.
If `binary` is true, the file is opened in binary mode. Otherwise it is opened in non-binary mode.
If the file does not exist or can not be read, an exception is thrown.
Operations on the returned `FileInput` handle read on the opened file.
File handles should be closed via `FileInput.close` once the operation is complete.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

write.haxe_doc:
Returns an `FileOutput` handle to the file specified by `path`.
If `binary` is true, the file is opened in binary mode. Otherwise it is opened in non-binary mode.
If the file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
Operations on the returned `FileOutput` handle write to the opened file. If the file existed, its previous content is overwritten.
File handles should be closed via `FileOutput.close` once the operation is complete.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

copy.haxe_doc:
Copies the contents of the file specified by `srcPath` to the file specified by `dstPath`.
If the `srcPath` does not exist or cannot be read, or if the `dstPath` file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
If the file at `dstPath` exists, its contents are overwritten.
If `srcPath` or `dstPath` are null, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
API for reading and writing files.
See `sys.FileSystem` for the complementary file system API.
Use `sys.io.File.read` to create a `FileInput`.
Use `sys.io.File.write` to create a `FileOutput`.

add.haxe_doc:
Adds an element at the end of `this` Deque.
(Java,Jvm): throws `java.lang.NullPointerException` if `i` is `null`.

push.haxe_doc:
Adds an element at the front of `this` Deque.
(Java,Jvm): throws `java.lang.NullPointerException` if `i` is `null`.

pop.haxe_doc:
Tries to retrieve an element from the front of `this` Deque.
If an element is available, it is removed from the queue and returned.
If no element is available and `block` is `false`, `null` is returned.
Otherwise, execution blocks until an element is available and returns it.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Deque instance which is initially empty.

class.haxe_doc: A Deque is a double-ended queue with a `pop` method that can block until an element is available. It is commonly used to synchronize threads.

Now.haxe_doc: There's already an event waiting to be executed

AnyTime.haxe_doc: An event is expected to arrive at any time. If `time` is specified, then the event will be ready at that time for sure.

At.haxe_doc: An event is expected to be ready for execution at `time`.

enum.haxe_doc: When an event loop has an available event to execute.

wait.haxe_doc: Waits for the lock to be released, or `timeout` (in seconds) to expire. Returns `true` if the lock is released and `false` if a time-out occurs.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new Lock which is initially locked.

hue.haxe_doc: * Gets or sets the hue in degrees. Assignments update RGB while preserving the other color components.

normalizedRed.haxe_doc: * Gets or sets the red channel normalized to the range 0-1.

flashOrigins.haxe_doc: * Original color transforms saved before sprites are flashed.

blink.haxe_doc: * Shows or hides a sprite according to a 50% duty-cycle blink. * A non-positive frequency leaves the sprite visible. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param elapsedTime The elapsed time in seconds. * @param frequency The number of blink cycles per second.

setVisible.haxe_doc: * Sets a sprite's visibility. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param visible Whether the sprite should be rendered.

setAlpha.haxe_doc: * Sets a sprite's opacity, clamped to 0-1. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param alpha The opacity.

flashColor.haxe_doc: * Updates an OpenFL sprite's color flash for the current frame. * `elapsedTime` is the time since the flash began. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param color The target flash color. * @param elapsedTime The time elapsed since the flash began, in seconds. * @param duration The total duration of the flash in seconds.

setPosition.haxe_doc: * Sets a sprite's position. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param x The horizontal position. * @param y The vertical position.

moveBy.haxe_doc: * Moves a sprite by an offset. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param x The horizontal offset. * @param y The vertical offset.

setScale.haxe_doc: * Sets a sprite's horizontal and vertical scale. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param x The horizontal scale. * @param y The vertical scale.

setRotation.haxe_doc: * Sets a sprite's rotation in degrees. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param degrees The clockwise rotation.

setFlipX.haxe_doc: * Sets whether a sprite is horizontally flipped. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param flipped Whether to flip the sprite.

setFlipY.haxe_doc: * Sets whether a sprite is vertically flipped. * @param sprite The sprite to update. * @param flipped Whether to flip the sprite.

int.haxe_doc: * Converts a boolean value to its integer representation. * @param bool The value to convert. * @return `1` for `true` or `0` for `false`.

toggle.haxe_doc: * Returns the opposite of a boolean value. * @param bool The value to toggle. * @return `false` for `true` or `true` for `false`.

xor.haxe_doc: * Returns whether exactly one of the two values is `true`. * @param bool The first value. * @param other The second value. * @return `true` when the values differ.

xnor.haxe_doc: * Returns whether both values are `false` or both are `true`. * @param bool The first value. * @param other The second value. * @return `true` when the values are equal.

nand.haxe_doc: * Returns the negation of the logical AND of two values. * @param bool The first value. * @param other The second value. * @return `false` only when both values are `true`.

nor.haxe_doc: * Returns the negation of the logical OR of two values. * @param bool The first value. * @param other The second value. * @return `true` only when both values are `false`.

implies.haxe_doc: * Checks whether the second value follows logically from the first. * @param bool The premise. * @param other The conclusion. * @return `false` only when the premise is `true` and the conclusion is `false`.

choose.haxe_doc: * Selects a value based on this boolean. * @param bool The condition. * @param whenTrue The value returned when `bool` is `true`. * @param whenFalse The value returned when `bool` is `false`. * @return The value corresponding to `bool`.

float.haxe_doc: * Converts a boolean to its floating-point representation. * @param bool The value to convert. * @return `1.0` for `true` or `0.0` for `false`.

fromInt.haxe_doc: * Converts a nonzero integer to `true` and zero to `false`. * @param int The value to convert. * @return `true` when `int` is nonzero.

when.haxe_doc: * Runs an action only when this value is `true`. * @param bool The condition. * @param action The action to run when `bool` is `true`.

unless.haxe_doc: * Runs an action only when this value is `false`. * @param bool The condition. * @param action The action to run when `bool` is `false`.

string.haxe_doc: * Converts a boolean to a string, optionally using custom text for each value. * @param bool The value to convert. * @param yes The string to return when `bool` is `true`; used only when `no` is also provided. * @param no The string to return when `bool` is `false`; used only when `yes` is also provided. * @return The matching custom string when both `yes` and `no` are provided; otherwise, the standard boolean string.

class.haxe_doc: * Utility methods for converting and transforming boolean values.

clamp.haxe_doc: * Restricts a number to the inclusive interval from `min` to `max`. * @param f The value to clamp. * @param min The lower bound. * @param max The upper bound. * @return The clamped value.

roundToDecimal.haxe_doc: * Rounds a number to a specified number of decimal places. * @param f The value to round. * @param d The number of decimal places. * @return The rounded value.

floorToDecimal.haxe_doc: * Rounds a number down to a specified number of decimal places. * @param f The value to round. * @param d The number of decimal places. * @return The rounded-down value.

ceilToDecimal.haxe_doc: * Rounds a number up to a specified number of decimal places. * @param f The value to round. * @param d The number of decimal places. * @return The rounded-up value.

lerp.haxe_doc: * Linearly interpolates between two numbers. * @param a The starting value. * @param b The ending value. * @param t The interpolation factor, clamped to the range 0-1. * @return The interpolated value.

fixedLerp.haxe_doc: * Interpolates toward a target with a factor adjusted for the current frame time. * The result is independent of frame rate when called once per frame with a consistent `t`. * @param a The starting value. * @param b The target value. * @param t The interpolation factor for a 60 FPS frame, clamped to the range 0-1. * @return The frame-time-adjusted interpolated value.

easeLerp.haxe_doc: * Interpolates between two numbers using an optional easing function. * @param a The starting value. * @param b The target value. * @param t The interpolation factor, clamped to the range 0-1. * @param e The optional easing function applied to the clamped factor. * @return The interpolated value.

fixedEaseLerp.haxe_doc: * Interpolates between two numbers using a frame-time-adjusted factor and an optional easing function. * @param a The starting value. * @param b The target value. * @param t The per-frame interpolation factor, clamped to the range 0-1 before frame-time adjustment. * @param e The optional easing function applied to the adjusted factor. * @return The interpolated value.

sign.haxe_doc: * Returns the sign of a number. * @param f The number to inspect. * @return `1` for positive values, `-1` for negative values, and `0` for zero.

randomSign.haxe_doc: * Chooses a random sign value. * @return `-1`, `0`, or `1`, each with equal probability.

class.haxe_doc: * Extension methods for common floating-point operations.

clamp.haxe_doc: * Restricts an integer to the inclusive interval from `min` to `max`. * @param int The value to clamp. * @param min The lower bound. * @param max The upper bound. * @return The clamped value.

sign.haxe_doc: * Returns the sign of an integer. * @param int The integer to inspect. * @return `1` for positive values, `-1` for negative values, and `0` for zero.

randomSign.haxe_doc: * Chooses a random sign value, excluding zero. * @return `-1` or `1`, each with equal probability.

isEven.haxe_doc: * Checks whether an integer is divisible by two. * @param int The integer to check. * @return `true` if the integer is even.

isOdd.haxe_doc: * Checks whether an integer is not divisible by two. * @param int The integer to check. * @return `true` if the integer is odd.

wrap.haxe_doc: * Wraps an integer outside the given bounds to the opposite bound. * Values already within the bounds are returned unchanged. * @param int The integer to wrap. * @param min The lower bound. * @param max The upper bound. * @return `max` if `int` is below `min`, `min` if it is above `max`, or `int` otherwise.

loop.haxe_doc: * Advances an integer to the next index in a zero-based sequence, wrapping at `max`. * @param int The current index. * @param max The positive number of indices in the sequence; must be greater than zero. * @return The next index in the range from 0 to `max - 1`.

between.haxe_doc: * Checks whether an integer falls within a range. * @param int The integer to check. * @param min The lower bound. * @param max The upper bound, which must be greater than or equal to `min`. * @param inclusive Whether the bounds are included; defaults to `true`. * @return `true` if `int` is within the range according to `inclusive`.

abs.haxe_doc: * Returns the absolute value of an integer. * @param int The integer to convert. * @return The non-negative magnitude of `int`.

digits.haxe_doc: * Counts the decimal digits in an integer, excluding its sign. * @param int The integer to inspect. * @return The number of decimal digits; returns `1` for zero.

padLeft.haxe_doc: * Converts an integer to a string padded on the left to a minimum length. * @param int The integer to convert. * @param length The minimum resulting string length. * @param char The string used for padding; defaults to `"0"`. * @return The padded integer string.

random.haxe_doc: * Chooses a random integer from the inclusive range `min` to `max`. * @param min The lower bound, which must be less than or equal to `max`. * @param max The upper bound. * @return A randomly selected integer in the range.

class.haxe_doc: * Utility methods for common integer operations.

first.haxe_doc: * Returns the first element of an array. * @param array The array to read. * @return The first element, or `null` when the array is empty.

last.haxe_doc: * Returns the last element of an array. * @param array The array to read. * @return The last element, or `null` when the array is empty.

clear.haxe_doc: * Removes all elements from an array. With the `flixel` define, also destroys each popped element as a `FlxBasic`. * @param array The array to clear.

clone.haxe_doc: * Creates a shallow copy of an array. * @param array The array to copy. * @return A new array containing the same elements.

sum.haxe_doc: * Adds the values in a non-empty numeric array. For a non-numeric array, returns its length. * @param array The array to sum. * @return The numeric total or array length, or `null` when the array is empty.

sub.haxe_doc: * Subtracts each remaining value in a non-empty numeric array from its first value. * For a non-numeric array, returns the negative array length. * @param array The array to subtract. * @return The result, or `null` when the array is empty.

nextItem.haxe_doc: * Returns the item following `curItem`, or the first item when wrapping from the end. * @param array The array to read. * @param curItem The current item index. * @param wrap Whether to return the first item when `curItem` is the last index. * @return The next item, or `null` when the array is empty, the index is invalid, or wrapping is disabled at the end.

previousItem.haxe_doc: * Returns the item preceding `curItem`, or the last item when wrapping from the start. * @param array The array to read. * @param curItem The current item index. * @param wrap Whether to return the last item when `curItem` is the first index. * @return The previous item, or `null` when the array is empty, the index is invalid, or wrapping is disabled at the start.

isArrayOf.haxe_doc: * Checks whether every element in an array is an instance of a type. * @param array The array to inspect. * @param type The type to check against. * @return `true` if every element matches, `false` if one does not, or `null` for an empty array.

sample.haxe_doc: * Selects up to `n` random elements without replacement, leaving the source array unchanged. * @param array The array to sample. * @param n The maximum number of elements to select. * @return The selected elements, or an empty array if the source is empty or `n` is not positive.

pluck.haxe_doc: * Reads a named field from every array element. * @param array The array of objects to read. * @param key The reflected field name. * @return An array containing the field values.

without.haxe_doc: * Creates a new array without elements whose values occur in `values`, preserving order. * @param array The source array, which is not modified. * @param values The values to exclude. * @return The source elements not found in `values`, or a copy of `array` when `values` is empty.

hasItems.haxe_doc: * Checks whether an array contains at least one element. * @param array The array to check. * @return `true` if the array is non-empty.

chunk.haxe_doc: * Splits an array into consecutive chunks of the requested size. * @param array The array to split. * @param size The positive maximum number of elements per chunk; must be greater than zero. * @return The resulting chunks in their original order.

class.haxe_doc: * Extension methods for reading, transforming, and managing arrays.

getOrElse.haxe_doc: * Gets a value from a map or returns a fallback when the key is absent. * @param map The map to read. * @param key The key to look up. * @param defaultValue The value to return if the key does not exist. * @return The mapped value or the fallback value.

getOrSet.haxe_doc: * Gets a value from a map or invokes an optional factory when the key is absent. * @param map The map to read and potentially modify. * @param key The key to look up or insert. * @param defaultFactory The optional factory invoked when the key is absent; a non-null result is stored in the map. * @return The existing value, the factory result, or `null` when the key is absent and no factory is provided.

merge.haxe_doc: * Creates a map containing the entries of both maps, with `otherMap` taking precedence. * @param map The source map. * @param otherMap The map whose entries override matching keys from `map`. * @return A new map containing the merged entries.

clone.haxe_doc: * Creates a shallow copy of a map. * @param map The map to copy. * @return A new map containing the same keys and values.

hasItems.haxe_doc: * Checks whether a map contains at least one key. * @param map The map to check. * @return `true` if the map has at least one entry.

toArray.haxe_doc: * Converts map entries into an array, skipping entries whose value is `null`. * @param map The map to convert. * @param f Converts a key and its non-null value into an array element. * @return An array of converted values.

keysArray.haxe_doc: * Returns a map's keys as an array. * @param map The map to read. * @return An array containing the map's keys.

valuesArray.haxe_doc: * Returns a map's values as an array. * @param map The map to read. * @return An array containing the map's values, or an empty array for an empty map.

isMapKeysOf.haxe_doc: * Checks whether all keys in a non-empty map are instances of a type. * @param map The map to inspect. * @param type The type to check against. * @return `true` if every key matches, `false` if one does not, or `null` for an empty map.

isMapValuesOf.haxe_doc: * Checks whether all values in a non-empty map are instances of a type. * @param map The map to inspect. * @param type The type to check against. * @return `true` if every value matches, `false` if one does not, or `null` for an empty map.

class.haxe_doc: * Extension methods for looking up, copying, transforming, and inspecting maps.

lerpColor.haxe_doc: * Interpolates between two ARGB colors using the supplied ratio directly. * @param color1 The starting ARGB color. * @param color2 The target ARGB color. * @param ratio The interpolation ratio; resulting channels are clamped to the range 0-255. * @return The interpolated ARGB color.

fixedLerpColor.haxe_doc: * Interpolates between two ARGB colors using a frame-rate-adjusted ratio. * @param color1 The starting ARGB color. * @param color2 The target ARGB color. * @param ratio The interpolation ratio, clamped to the range 0-1 before frame-rate adjustment. * @return The interpolated ARGB color.

easeLerpColor.haxe_doc: * Interpolates between two ARGB colors using an optional easing function. * @param color1 The starting ARGB color. * @param color2 The target ARGB color. * @param ratio The interpolation ratio, passed to `ease` when provided; resulting channels are clamped to 0-255. * @param ease The optional easing function applied to the ratio. * @return The interpolated ARGB color.

fixedEaseLerpColor.haxe_doc: * Interpolates between two ARGB colors using a frame-time-adjusted ratio and optional easing function. * @param color1 The starting ARGB color. * @param color2 The target ARGB color. * @param ratio The interpolation ratio, clamped to 0-1 before frame-time adjustment. * @param ease The optional easing function applied to the adjusted ratio. * @return The interpolated ARGB color.

fromRgb.haxe_doc: * Creates an opaque ARGB color from red, green, and blue channels in the range 0-255. * Values outside that range are clamped. * @param r The red channel. * @param g The green channel. * @param b The blue channel. * @return The packed ARGB color with alpha set to 255.

getAlpha.haxe_doc: * Returns the alpha channel of an ARGB color. * @param color The ARGB color to inspect. * @return The alpha channel as a value from 0 to 255.

getRed.haxe_doc: * Returns the red channel of an ARGB color. * @param color The ARGB color to inspect. * @return The red channel as a value from 0 to 255.

getGreen.haxe_doc: * Returns the green channel of an ARGB color. * @param color The ARGB color to inspect. * @return The green channel as a value from 0 to 255.

getBlue.haxe_doc: * Returns the blue channel of an ARGB color. * @param color The ARGB color to inspect. * @return The blue channel as a value from 0 to 255.

toString.haxe_doc: * Converts an ARGB color integer to its decimal string representation. * @param color The ARGB color to convert. * @return The decimal representation of `color`.

class.haxe_doc: * Utility methods for creating, interpolating, and reading ARGB colors.

getNames.haxe_doc: * Returns the constructor names of an enum. * @param e The enum type to inspect. * @return The constructor names, or an empty array when `e` is `null`.

fromString.haxe_doc: * Creates an enum value from its constructor name. * @param e The enum type. * @param name The constructor name. * @param defaultValue The value to return if the enum or constructor name is invalid. * @return The created enum value, or `defaultValue` if it cannot be created.

fromIndex.haxe_doc: * Creates an enum value from its constructor index. * @param e The enum type. * @param index The zero-based constructor index. * @param defaultValue The value to return if the enum or index is invalid. * @return The created enum value, or `defaultValue` if it cannot be created.

toIndex.haxe_doc: * Returns the constructor index of an enum value. * @param enumValue The enum value to inspect. * @return The zero-based constructor index, or `-1` if the value is `null`.

toString.haxe_doc: * Returns the constructor name of an enum value. * @param enumValue The enum value to inspect. * @return The constructor name, or an empty string if the value is `null`.

getAllValues.haxe_doc: * Creates every enum constructor that can be instantiated without arguments. * @param e The enum type to inspect. * @return The created values; constructors requiring arguments are skipped.

class.haxe_doc: * Reflection helpers for enum types and values.

isBlank.haxe_doc: * Checks whether a string is `null`, empty, or contains only whitespace. * @param str The string to check. * @return `true` if the string is `null`, empty, or blank after trimming.

truncate.haxe_doc: * Truncates a string when its length exceeds a threshold. The threshold controls the prefix length, not the final * length when a suffix is appended. * @param str The string to truncate. * @param maxLength The length threshold and prefix limit; values less than or equal to zero produce an empty string. * @param suffix The text appended after truncation; defaults to `"..."`. * @return The original string if it fits, an empty string if `maxLength` is not positive, or the first * `maxLength - 1` characters followed by `suffix`. The suffix can make the result longer than `maxLength`.

reverse.haxe_doc: * Reverses the order of the characters in a string. * @param str The string to reverse. * @return A new string with the characters in reverse order.

stripPrefix.haxe_doc: * Removes the specified prefix if the string starts with it. * @param str The string to inspect. * @param prefix The prefix to remove. * @return The string without `prefix` when it starts with it; otherwise, the original string.

stripSuffix.haxe_doc: * Removes the specified suffix if the string ends with it. * @param str The string to inspect. * @param suffix The suffix to remove. * @return The string without `suffix` when it ends with it; otherwise, the original string.

toTitleCase.haxe_doc: * Converts a string to title case, separating words at whitespace, hyphens, and underscores. * Each word starts with an uppercase letter and continues in lowercase; separators become spaces. * @param str The string to convert. * @return The title-cased string.

toCamelCase.haxe_doc: * Converts a string to camel case, separating words at whitespace, hyphens, and underscores. * @param str The string to convert. * @param type Whether the first word starts in lowercase (`Lower`) or uppercase (`Upper`); defaults to `Lower`. * @return The camel-cased string with separators removed.

toKebabCase.haxe_doc: * Converts whitespace-, hyphen-, and underscore-separated words to kebab case. * Leading and trailing separators are removed, and consecutive separators become one hyphen. * @param str The string to convert. * @param type Whether the result is lowercase (`Lower`) or uppercase (`Upper`); defaults to `Lower`. * @return The converted string with words separated by hyphens.

toSnakeCase.haxe_doc: * Converts whitespace-, hyphen-, and underscore-separated words to snake case. * Leading and trailing separators are removed, and consecutive separators become one underscore. * @param str The string to convert. * @param type Whether the result is lowercase (`Lower`) or uppercase (`Upper`); defaults to `Lower`. * @return The converted string with words separated by underscores.

class.haxe_doc: * Utility methods for checking, transforming, and formatting strings.

enum.haxe_doc: * Selects the letter case used when converting strings.

PI2.haxe_doc: * Half-pi constant used by sine and cosine easing formulas.

EL.haxe_doc: * Angular frequency used by the elastic easing formulas.

B1.haxe_doc: * First breakpoint in the piecewise bounce-out curve.

B2.haxe_doc: * Second breakpoint in the piecewise bounce-out curve.

B3.haxe_doc: * Offset used by the second segment of the bounce-out curve.

B4.haxe_doc: * Third breakpoint in the piecewise bounce-out curve.

B5.haxe_doc: * Offset used by the third segment of the bounce-out curve.

B6.haxe_doc: * Offset used by the final segment of the bounce-out curve.

ELASTIC_AMPLITUDE.haxe_doc: * Amplitude used by the elastic easing formulas.

ELASTIC_PERIOD.haxe_doc: * Oscillation period used by the elastic easing formulas.

ELASTIC_IN_START.haxe_doc: * Elastic ease-in value at progress zero, used for endpoint normalization.

ELASTIC_IN_END.haxe_doc: * Elastic ease-in value at progress one, used for endpoint normalization.

ELASTIC_OUT_START.haxe_doc: * Elastic ease-out value at progress zero, used for endpoint normalization.

ELASTIC_OUT_END.haxe_doc: * Elastic ease-out value at progress one, used for endpoint normalization.

linear.haxe_doc: * Returns the interpolation progress unchanged. * @param t The interpolation progress value. * @return The eased progress value.

quad.haxe_doc: * Applies the quadratic easing curve using the selected direction. * @param t The interpolation progress value. * @param type The easing direction; defaults to `InOut`. * @return The eased progress value.

Defaults to `en-US`. * @return The date formatted as month/day/year for `en-US`, year/month/day for Japanese or Chinese * locales (with slashes) and Korean locales (with dots), or day/month/year for other locales. * German and Russian locales use dots as separators.
